text:
incident-bot: SEV2 page triggered: increased retransmits across IB fabric affecting serving clusters (region-us-west-2). auto-attach: paging SREs and infra.
maya: paging received, jumping in. seeing ~12% retransmit rate on 3 top racks.
ben: confirmed. PGs showing packet_retransmit counter spiking. some serving jobs with repeated KV cache misses and higher tail latency.
sam: service alerts - error spike in runtime: "container restart loop" and occasional CUDA timeout logs. correlates with IB spikes.
ekaterina: any customer-facing impact? CPU slots show elevated retry rate but no 5xx across most tenants yet. a handful of dedicated customers show model latency >2s.
maya: customer-impact: 3 dedicated customers reported degraded throughput, one reported timeouts on long-context requests. marking P2.
ben: I'm pulling ibstat and perf counters now. attaching quick output below.
ben: ```
# from node gpu-rack-12
ibstat mlx5_0
    link_state: Active
    rate: 100Gb

# counters
portx_retransmits: 12890
portx_unrecoverable: 4
packets_rx_drop: 310
```

sam: thanks. running `tcptraceroute` like checks between affected nodes shows intermittent retransmit windows. suspect ECN reaction or PCIe stall.
ekaterina: infra-bot, any recent config changes to fabric or jumbo mtu?
infra-bot: deployment 1924999999 applied a kernel net driver update to rack-12 earlier today, rollouts staged. no config changes to MTU.
maya: ok, roll forward plan? can we fail traffic to fallback path?
ben: we have routing policy that can move traffic to region-us-east-1 or to non-RDMA fallback. I'll start moving non-latency-critical replicas to fallback pool.
sam: initiating canary redirect for serving-v2 across 10% traffic to fallback (kernel tcp). command: `infractl route set --service serving-v2 --policy fallback-nonrdma --percent 10`
maya: runbook step: drain GPU nodes with high retran metrics to avoid thrash. ben, can you start drain on gpu-rack-12-node-7?
ben: draining node now: `k8s cordon gpu-rack-12-node-7 && kubectl drain gpu-rack-12-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
ekaterina: are we seeing OOM / CUDA errors tied to restarts? any correlation with kube eviction?
sam: logs from a restarted container: ```
[2025-11-07T15:12:03Z] runtime: cuda error: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT
[2025-11-07T15:12:03Z] serving: kvcache flush triggered
[2025-11-07T15:12:04Z] container: restarted (exit_code=137)
```

ben: exit_code=137 likely OOM kill after kernel stalled. draining should reduce churn.
maya: paging team to contact account owner for the affected dedicated customer, add to incident timeline. ekaterina, Sam, Ben — I'll take coordination with customer support.
ekaterina: I'll open an incident incident channel for the customer and loop CS.
pagerduty: On-call handoff scheduled: sam takes 15:20-15:50 window. handoff note: fabric degrad, draining nodes, traffic fallback at 10%.
sam: received handoff, I'll be primary. maya you remain incident lead.
maya: accepted. next steps: 1) escalate fabric team to run link-level diagnostics/clear CRC errors, 2) continue incremental traffic fallback to 30% if tail p95 doesn't improve, 3) monitor container restarts and pause any automatic rollout jobs.
ben: running `ibdiagnet` and will kick continuous probe across affected paths. output showing intermittent lane errors on link 3/4 on mlx5_0.
ben: ```
[ib_err] lane3_crc_err: 7
[ib_err] lane4_crc_err: 5
[link_status] flit_err_threshold: crossed
```
ekaterina: fabric team asked to reseat QSFP on spine-2 and replace transceiver on leaf-7. ETA 25m.
maya: plan to avoid full region failover — prefer incremental fallback + canary to other regions. Sam, prepare rolling restart exclusion for serving controller so we don't trigger rolling restarts during this instability.
sam: set `deployment.serving-controller.autoroll=false` in cluster cfg. applied.
infra-bot: routing change success: serving-v2 10% routed to fallback-nonrdma at 15:23:02Z.
ben: after reseat, lane CRC errors dropped to 0 on spine-2 but leaf-7 still shows occasional errors.
ekaterina: fabric ops performing deeper PHY diagnostics, seeing temperature spikes on leaf-7 QSFP. they suggest swap.
maya: ok swap scheduled. meanwhile let's increase fallback to 25% to relieve pressure. sam run: `infractl route set --service serving-v2 --percent 25`
sam: done at 15:35Z. p95 for affected customers dropped from 2.3s -> 1.1s. retries down ~60%.
ben: node restart loops reduced after drains and fallback. no new CUDA timeout logs in last 12m.
maya: customer impact update for CS: degraded but improving, we've applied partial traffic fallback and draining. ETA for full stabilization 30m pending hardware swap.
ekaterina: hardware swap completed at 15:50Z, leaf-7 QSFP replaced. fabric counters normalizing.
infra-bot: link metrics: retransmit rate back to baseline (<0.5%).
sam: increased traffic fallback back down from 25% -> 5% to reduce cross-region latency. `infractl route set --service serving-v2 --percent 5`
maya: monitoring for 15 more minutes. if stable, we'll close pager.
ben: check on remaining node: gpu-rack-12-node-7 remained drained and will be rejoined after 2 successful health checks.
ekaterina: CS notified customers of mitigation and estimated full resolution.
pagerduty: incident severity downgraded to P3 at 16:05Z after sustained stabilization.
maya: postmortem owners: ben (fabric diagnostics), sam (runtime resilience), ekaterina (customer comms + timeline). I'll file initial incident doc and timeline.
ben: adding notes: consider automated detection for persistent lane CRC + temperature correlation to trigger proactive reseat.
sam: also consider disabling autoroll during IB anomalies or exposing an API flag to pause rollout.
maya: thanks everyone. closing channel for now, keeping monitoring open for 1h. reacting with :white_check_mark:.
